name: Paul Leim
notes: The metronomic pole of Nashville session drumming, and the entry frames it as the archetype's other end: "the reference for machine-tight timing played by hand, which is what makes a 150-BPM two-beat usable as a dance record". That sentence gives the tempo centre, so `bpm.mode` is 150 inside the stated 60–175 band. The identity is a single sourced characterisation — a studio owner's description that he played "as if he had a metronome in his head" — with the entry's own translation: "timing variance near zero and velocity drift near zero on the stream, with expression coming from the accent map rather than from rubato — the opposite of the anticipated, ahead-of-the-grid bluegrass feel documented earlier in this section, and therefore the archetype's other pole". So `humanize.quantizeStrength` is 0.99 with 1 ms of jitter on every lane and `velocityVar` 0.03, which is the tightest setting anywhere in this section, and no `snare.offGridMs` is authored at all — the parent's 0 is exactly right and every other model here moves off it. The expression lives in the accent map instead: `velocityTiers.accent` 112–127 over a narrow 80–92 main band. "Pattern-preserving throughout; fills at 8- and 16-bar boundaries only; no groove variation across a track" is `fills` 8/16, `hihat.fillDensity` 0.022 and `arrangement.transitions.switchUpProb` 0. The bass is stated: "his records lock bass to kick on 1 and 3 with no float", i.e. `rhythm` mirror_kick at `followRootsProb` 0.72 — the two-beat’s root on 1 and fifth on 3 — with `anticipationProb` 0.02, the flattest placement in this section. ⚠ His entry gives no keys ("n/a") and no scale preference, so neither is authored and both inherit from the genre. ⚠ The chords and melody blocks are INFERRED, and the inference is stated rather than hidden: the entry documents only a credit range (Shania Twain, Randy Travis, Kenny Rogers, Lionel Richie, Amy Grant, plus film and TV) and says "the same tight two-beat is documented working under pop and AC arrangements as well as country ones", so a mainstream I–IV–V / I–V–vi–IV vocabulary and a plain mid-register topline are this author's reading of that roster, not a researched fact. That sentence names no 2000s-radio or teen-pop record — the credits it rests on are country, AC and film/TV — so `relatedGenres` stays inside the country lanes and no pop link is authored. ⚠ Also INFERRED: the exact velocity numbers and `percs` contents. The entry rates itself medium-high, with the timing characterisation and the award record sourced and the parameterisation a direct reading of that characterisation. ⚠ **`anticipationProb` is deliberately left at 0.02, and the variety this model owed came from pitch instead.** The research is explicit — *"his records lock bass to kick on 1 and 3 **with no float**"* — so pushing the bass a sixteenth early would have contradicted the one sourced sentence about his low end. It measured **388 distinct basslines in 1,000 seeds** against `bass.rs`'s floor of 500, and the cause was that a two-onset bar over a fixed kick with `followRootsProb` 0.97 has almost nothing to vary. `followRootsProb` 0.72 is the Nashville two-beat this section's own grammar block describes — root on 1, fifth on 3 — rather than a walking line, and the register's top moves 42 → 44 so more than three pitch classes have a second octave inside it (still under `country-train`'s `chords.voicing.register` [45, 74]). ⚠ **INFERRED:** the exact 0.72 and the `m7` beside `P5` and `M2` are archetype-conventional, not sourced — his entry's bass line is `n/a` apart from the kick lock.
